note: DELIBERATELY CORRUPTED teaching material for the Week 5 data-validation lab. Values have been edited. Never train on this file.

cell_faults.why: A non-numeric string in a numeric column. Whoever exported this file used a sentinel word instead of an empty cell, which turns the whole column into text.
Nobody is 250 years old. A plausible-looking integer in a column with no upper bound declared.
A negative concentration. Often a sentinel for 'not measured' picked by whoever wrote the export, with nobody downstream told.
A third class in a binary target. Silently trains a model on a label that does not exist.
An empty cell where the contract says a value is required.
BMI multiplied by ten, as if the exporter switched units or dropped a decimal separator. THE SUBTLE ONE: still numeric, still positive, invisible to a row count.
Second occurrence of the same unit change, so the report shows a pattern rather than a one-off typo.
A date that cannot exist. Month 13, day 45 — the kind of thing a hand-edited spreadsheet produces.

file_faults.why: A column nobody agreed to. Harmless here, but it means the producer changed the file without telling the consumer — and the next change might not be harmless.
An exact copy of row 5. Double-counts one patient in training and in the metrics.
